title: ENSO adjustment reduced shared warm-month counts from 27 to 17 in two tropical ocean boxes in 1950-2025
abstract: We tested shared warm months in a North tropical Atlantic box and a tropical Indian Ocean box with NOAA ERSSTv5 for 1950-2025. After month-specific linear trends were removed, the two boxes shared 27 top-decile warm months out of 912. An added adjustment for mean Nino 3.4 anomalies at lags three to six months reduced the count to 17. Thresholds were set separately for each month, box and model. Excess joint frequency above a whole-year shift mean fell by 1.11 percentage points. Its conditional 95% five-year block interval was 0.24 to 2.11 points. A quadratic-trend check had an interval that included zero. With coefficients fitted through 1987, later shared counts fell from 16 to 7 in 1988-2025. This is a limited statistical benchmark for an established ENSO link, not proof of a physical cause or of no residual dependence. One product, two selected boxes, sparse tails, slow climate change, and intervals that hold fits and thresholds fixed limit inference. Code, aggregate inputs, source hashes, numerical audits and repeat instructions are included.

display.caption: Shared warm months before and after ENSO adjustment. The dashed line is the baseline year-shift mean. Right: excess overlap reduction and conditional 95% five-year block intervals. Fits and thresholds are held fixed. The quadratic-trend interval includes zero.
